title: Department of Veterans Affairs Contracting Preference Consistency Act of 2020
official_summary:
Department of Veterans Affairs Contracting Preference Consistency Act of 2020

This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to give preference to nonprofit firms that employ the blind and significantly disabled when contracting for covered products and services that are included on the procurement list maintained by the U.S. AbilityOne Commission. The commission provides employment opportunities for people who are blind or have significant disabilities.

The bill provides an exemption in certain situations for covered products or services for which contracts were awarded after December 22, 2006, and were in effect on the day before the enactment date of this bill.

A covered product or service is one that was included on the commission's procurement list on or before December 22, 2006, or a product or service that (1) is a replacement for a product or service on the commission's procurement list, (2) is essentially the same and meets the same requirements as the product or service being replaced, and (3) meets the VA's quality standards and delivery schedule.

summary.headline: This law requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to give preference to certain nonprofit firms that employ blind or significantly disabled workers when buying products and services on a specific federal list.
summary.what_it_does: The VA must favor nonprofit firms that employ people who are blind or have significant disabilities when it buys covered products and services. Those items must be on the procurement list kept by the U.S. AbilityOne Commission, which creates jobs for these workers. The law also has an exception for certain contracts that were awarded after December 22, 2006 and were still in effect the day before the law was enacted. It also covers replacement products that are essentially the same as listed items and meet VA quality standards and delivery schedules.

who_it_affects.group: Nonprofit firms that employ blind or significantly disabled workers
who_it_affects.how: These firms get preference when they compete for VA contracts for items on the AbilityOne procurement list.
The law is intended to support job opportunities for these workers through VA purchasing of listed products and services.

who_it_affects.group: Other vendors that sell to the VA
who_it_affects.how: Vendors selling items on the AbilityOne procurement list may face more competition from qualifying nonprofits when the VA buys those items.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 8, 2020; the summary does not give a separate effective date.
